en.html:
About three minutes after leaving Yokohama, I caught sight of the enormous helium balloon swimming through the sky.

Not merely because we had guessed it would take a direct course. An airship could not tell the wind to mind its own business. Depending on the wind’s direction, it might be pushed well off course.

In fact, the ship had drifted a little south of its intended course. Our search had not wasted time because old Nagakura had foreseen this and prepared a transmitter.

Soon after departure, we had picked up the signal from the Captain and her attendant, already aboard. After that, follow it. Prediction and Muramasa’s radar alone would have taken longer.

Three minutes. Best we could ask for.
Now to get inside equally quickly, without wasting this good result—but—

ja.html:
横浜から飛び立って約三分。
　空を泳ぐ巨大なヘリウム風船を肉眼で確認する。

　この早さは飛行艦が目的地へ直進するという事前の
推測のみに起因しない。
　飛行艦は風を無視しては飛べない器械だ。風向次第
では針路を大きく逸らす事態も起こり得た。

　実際、船は予定針路をやや南へ外れている。
　さりながら捜索に時間を浪費しなかったのは、かく
あるを読んで永倉老が発信機を用意した事こそ大きい。

　船内に潜入済みの大鳥主従が発する信号を横浜出立
から間もなくして受信し、後はそれを辿って追う事が
できたのだった。
　予測と村正の<ruby>探査<rt>レーダー</rt></ruby>のみではもっと時間を食ったろう。

　三分での捕捉は<ruby>最善<rt>ベスト</rt></ruby>といえる。
　この折角の成果を無駄にしないため、突入も手早く
済ませてしまいたいが――

en.html:
An airship’s weak side was above.
The swollen gasbag blocked the view of anything approaching from there.

Their signal search had probably detected us. But enemy craft, large bird, or simple error? That identification should not come so easily.

　信号探査で<ruby>飛行体<rt>こちら</rt></ruby>の存在を察知してはいるだろうが、

The Vickers Mark IV was roughly a hundred and forty metres long. Beside the Graf Zeppelin, famous for going around the world, a child standing before an adult.

For us in a dragoon, however, the child was still a bloody castle in the air.

en.html:
Dread speared through me. I stopped my tsurugi from blaming herself.
Senile? Me. That honour was mine.

Captain Ootori had told me. A UNIT of stealth dragoons. A whole UNIT already existed!

Only one would join this operation. Only to drop the bomb. Nobody would use the others as invisible escorts for the airship—

WHO had promised me this? When? Kageaki, bhosdike, did a guarantee come down from heaven for your personal convenience!?

Even idiocy should have some limit...!

戦慄の槍に貫かれながら、劒冑の自責を差し止める。
　痴呆症に冒されているとすれば、それは俺だった。

　大鳥大尉は俺に教えていたのだ――
　隠形竜騎兵の『部隊』が既に存在すると！

　この作戦に使われるのはそのうち一騎だけ、爆弾の
投下に利用されるだけで、飛行艦の<ruby>見えざる護衛騎<rt>・・・・・・・</rt></ruby>と
して用いられることなどない――
　そんな約束をいつ、誰が、俺にしたのか!?

　間を抜かすにも程がある……！

en.html:
That way, both signal search and ordinary sight could miss them. Heat-source detection might have caught them... but my thinking had never reached that far.

Had it reached, perhaps I would have noticed before they came this close. There might have been time to reconsider our approach. Now? Too late.

At the moment when intelligence was required, I had brought this empty dabba of a head!

ja.html:
そうすれば信号探査も目視確認も回避できる。
　熱源探査でなら<ruby>捕捉<rt>キャッチ</rt></ruby>できたかもしれないが……俺が
そこまで知恵を回せなかった。

　その知恵があればここまで近付かれるまでに気付き、
突入方法を再考する選択もあったろうに。
　今となっては後の祭り。

　肝心な時にこう失態を晒すとは！

en.html:
Two armoured shapes closed in. Their movement told me enough about the riders’ skill and the machines’ performance.

Both extremely high.
Of course. The men had Cannon’s confidence and a share in his top-secret operation. The machines were the League forces’ newest ST-09s.

Winged Demons. For once, no exaggeration in the name.
In this situation, staying to fight them was not a sensible activity for us.

こちらに迫る騎影二つ。
　身ごなしを観察すれば、仕手の力量と騎体性能の程
は明らかだった。

　どちらも極めて高度。
　当然だ――前者はキャノン中佐が信任して極秘作戦
の一翼を担わせた人材、後者は国際連盟軍の最新鋭騎
ＳＴ-〇九なのだから。

　<ruby>空の悪魔<rt>ウイングドデーモン</rt></ruby>と呼ばれるに相応しい者ども。
　とてもの事、こんな状況下で戦っていられる相手で
はない。
